Definition: of Hebrew origin (H1583); Gamaliel (i.e. Gamliel), an Israelite:--Gamaliel.
BiblicalUsage: Gamaliel was a Pharisee, a doctor of the law, had in reputation among all the people. He stood up in the council in Acts 5:34 and commanded the apostles to be put forth a little space, then counselled restraint: if their work were of men it would fail, but if of God it could not be overthrown. Paul later said he was brought up at the feet of Gamaliel in Acts 22:3, taught according to the perfect manner of the law.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Gamaliel is the wise voice in a room full of anger. He counselled patience, and he taught Paul, and I hold that God uses a wise teacher's restraint to protect His church in its most dangerous hour.
